tagline: Five miles of farm road that was woods in March 1865.
intro: NC 82 leaves Godwin and runs five and a half miles over a low plateau between the floodplains of the Cape Fear and Black rivers, past small farms and patches of woods. That plateau is why Sherman's army came this way from Fayetteville in March 1865, bound for a Confederate munitions depot at Goldsboro. Lafayette had traveled the same road in 1825, and in the mid-1800s it was part of the plank road system, built of timber cut nearby.

On March 16 Hardee's Confederates met the Union left wing marching up the Raleigh plank road. They gave up two lines, held a third, and withdrew when they found themselves outnumbered. Three days later came Bentonville.

moments.title: Trench lines
moments.text: Just short of the Harnett County line a re-creation of the original trench lines runs through what was woodland in 1865 and is farmland now.

moments.title: Chicora Civil War Cemetery
moments.text: At the cemetery stands a restored cabin of an enslaved person from the Smith Plantation, which once held the land along the byway.

moments.title: Lebanon Plantation
moments.text: About a mile past the battlefield museum the red roof of Lebanon shows in a grove on the right, a Confederate hospital in 1865 and a private home now.
